production.note: US model years. First: Audi of America's 2016 TT brochure (the first 8S model year in the US). Last: Audi of America, 2 November 2023: "The Audi TT closes production after the 2023 model, ending a chapter of iconic design for the brand" (audi-us-tt-final-edition-2023).

body.note: TT Coupe. Audi also sold the open TT Roadster in the US (a separate column in the same tables, 3,395 lb in 2019); Audi markets it under its own name with its own model page (media.audiusa.com/models/tt-roadster), so it is left out of this record. TTS and TT RS are separate variants.

aspiration.note: 2.0 TFSI: a single turbocharger with direct injection.

transmission.note: 2019 on: 'Seven-speed S tronic® dual-clutch automatic transmission and quattro® all-wheel drive'. 2016 to 2018: 'Six-speed S tronic® dual-clutch transmission with quattro® all-wheel drive' (audi-us-2016-tt-brochure, audi-us-2018-tt-press-kit). S tronic is a DCT. No manual in the US.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower (@ rpm) 228 @ 5,000–6,700 228 @ 5,000–6,700 288 @ 5,400–6,200" (TT Coupe, TT Roadster, TTS). 2016 to 2018 the TT was rated 220 hp: "220 @ 4,500–6,200" (audi-us-2016-tt-brochure; 2018 press kit "220 @ 4,500-6,200 (162 kW)", audi-us-2018-tt-press-kit). 228 hp covers 2019 to 2023 (five of eight model years), so the reference year is 2019; Audi's 2021 sheet and the 2023 Final Edition release also give 228 hp (audi-us-2021-tt-techspecs, audi-us-tt-final-edition-2023).

weightLb.note: TT Coupe, 7-speed S tronic (the only transmission), 2019 model. Quote: "Curb weight (lb) 3,208 3,395 3,263" (TT Coupe, TT Roadster, TTS). Other Audi of America figures for the coupe: 3,186 lb (2016 brochure), 3,164 lb (2018 press kit), 3,197 lb (2021 sheet: 'Curb Weight (lbs) 3,197').
